examples.zh: 童子军每天都要完成一件好事。

examples.en: He took a deep breath before entering his boss's office.
examples.zh: 他在进老板办公室前深吸了一口气。

examples.en: The deep layers of the ocean are still almost unexplored.
examples.zh: 海洋的深层仍然几乎未被探索。

default.translation: n. 违约, 不履行责任, 缺席, 默认值\nv. 疏怠职责, 缺席, 拖欠, 默认\n[计] 默认; 默认值; 缺省值

examples.zh: 那些想要颠覆这个世界的人们，我们将击败你们。

examples.zh: 胜败不能单靠兵力多少。

examples.zh: 生命中你无法选择接踵而至的挑战，但是你可以选择不成为一个失败者。

n. an imperfection in a bodily system
n. a failing or deficiency

examples.en: To defend ourselves, we had to tell a lie.
examples.zh: 为了保护自己，我们只好说谎。

examples.en: The town was defended by a large army.
examples.zh: 城市由一支大军守卫。

examples.zh: 下个月就要进行硕士论文答辩了。

decadent.definition: n. a person who has fallen into a decadent state (morally or artistically)\ns. marked by excessive self-indulgence and moral decay
decadent.translation: a. 衰微的, 颓废的\nn. 颓废派

examples.en: The truffle risotto at Benedito's restaurant is decadent.
We indulged in a decadent chocolate cake.
The tiramisu at Benedito's restaurant is decadent.

decency.definition: n. the quality of conforming to standards of propriety and morality\nn. the quality of being polite and respectable
decency.translation: n. 得体, 礼貌, 正派\n[法] 正当, 正派, 合乎礼仪

examples.en: She had the decency to apologize.
examples.zh: 她大方地道歉。

words.tran: 正派的；得体的；相当好的
合适地；高雅地；正派地；亲切地

syno.tran: 正派；体面；庄重；合乎礼仪；礼貌

decimate.definition: v. kill one in every ten, as of mutineers in Roman armies
decimate.translation: vt. 每十人杀一人, 大批杀害

examples.en: Hezbollah has the potential to decimate Israeli forces inside Lebanon.
Our team will decimate yours on the field tomorrow.
Dmitri decimated every single soldier that came in his way.

decipher.translation: vt. 译解, 解释\nn. 密电译文

examples.en: Champollion deciphered the Ancient Egyptian language.
examples.zh: 商博良破译了古埃及语。

decrement.definition: n the amount by which something decreases\nn a process of becoming smaller or shorter
decrement.translation: n. 渐减, 减少, 减少量\n[计] 减量; 减

defiant.definition: a. boldly resisting authority or an opposing force
defiant.translation: a. 挑衅的, 目中无人的

examples.en: He often takes a defiant attitude toward us.
examples.zh: 他常以反抗的态度对我们。

degenerate.definition: n a person whose behavior deviates from what is acceptable especially in sexual behavior\nv grow worse\ns unrestrained by convention or morality
degenerate.translation: a. 堕落的\nvi. 退化, 堕落\nvt. 使变质, 使退化

examples.en: Live can so easily degenerate into something sordid and vulgar.
There remain great fears of seeing the clashes degenerate into massacres.
Though my uncle is homeless, I don't think he is a degenerate.

words.tran: 退化；[医] 变性；堕落；恶化
退化；[物] 简并；堕落；退步

deity.definition: n. any supernatural being worshipped as controlling some part of the world or some aspect of life or who is the personification of a force

examples.en: Do you know which deity this temple is dedicated to?
examples.zh: 您知道这座庙宇供奉的是哪个神吗？

delectable.definition: s. extremely pleasing to the sense of taste\ns. capable of arousing desire
delectable.translation: a. 令人快乐的, 美味的, 使人愉快的

examples.en: Delectable odors of ham and toast pervaded the air.
These muffins are nothing short of delectable!
This cake is delectable.

demeanor.definition: n. (behavioral attributes) the way a person behaves toward other people
demeanor.translation: 行为, 品行, 举止

examples.en: You reflect the calm of the ocean in your demeanor.
Your calm demeanor contrasts with my passionate approach to life.
Jamin's graceful posture and confident demeanor enhance her natural beauty.

demise.definition: v. transfer by a lease or by a will
demise.translation: n. 崩, 薨, 死亡\nvt. 让渡, 遗赠, 转让

examples.en: I will always be here for Tom until my demise.
Alienation from nature will one day become humanity's demise.
Rumours of our demise have been greatly exaggerated.

demolition.translation: n. 破坏, 毁坏, 撤销\n[经] 拆毁(除,破坏)

examples.en: This was the first time Tom had ever seen a demolition derby.
Settlers are now openly talking about the demolition of the Al-Aqsa Mosque.
This was the first time that Tom had ever seen a demolition derby.

denomination.definition: n. a group of religious congregations having its own organization and a distinctive faith\nn. a class of one kind of unit in a system of numbers or measures or weights or money
denomination.translation: n. 名称, 教派, 面额\n[经] 票面金额, 名称, (度量衡)

examples.en: Our denomination practices exclusive psalmody in worship.
Is the denomination "white man" racist?
When developing an ecumenical service, take care not to offend members of any denomination.

depot.definition: n station where transport vehicles load or unload passengers or goods\nn a depository for goods
depot.translation: n. 停车场, 车站, 贮藏所, 仓库\n[医] 仓库, 贮存, 积存

examples.en: I made a quick visit to the Home Depot.
I bought some in a bolt depot.
Claudio stopped at a Home Depot and bought a Christmas tree from there.

depreciate.definition: v. lower the value of something\nv. lose in value
depreciate.translation: vi. 贬值\nvt. 降价, 贬低

examples.en: Does the Algerian dinar have to be depreciated again?
Algeria shouldn't depreciate its national currency.
The Moroccan dirham is rapidly depreciating in value.
Layla lived in a remote and desolate part of Australia.
Yanni lives in a remote, desolate area in southern Algeria.
It was a thoroughly desolate landscape, without a soul in sight.

despatch.definition:
n an official report (usually sent in haste)
n the property of being prompt and efficient
n killing a person or animal
n the act of sending off something
v send away towards a designated goal

examples.en: I will remand the order I despatched to my banker.
By the end of this weekend past we had despatched enough food now to feed over 250,000 people.

detain.definition: v deprive of freedom; take into confinement\nv stop or halt\nv cause to be slowed down or delayed
detain.translation: vt. 扣留, 扣押, 耽搁\n[法] 拘留, 扣押, 留住

examples.en: My boss detained me more than 30 minutes.
examples.zh: 老板多留了我三十分钟。

detector.definition: n. any device that receives a signal or stimulus (as heat or pressure or light or motion etc.) and responds to it in a distinctive manner\nn. rectifier that extracts modulation from a radio carrier wave\nn. electronic equipment that detects the presence of radio signals or radioactivity
detector.translation: n. 发现者, 检验器, 检波器\n[计] 检波器; 检测器

examples.en: Every house should have at least one carbon monoxide detector.
Tom was asked to take a lie detector test.
I want to buy a really good smoke detector.

words.tran: 侦查，探测；发觉，发现；察觉

syno.tran: [自][电子]检测器；发现者；侦察器

phrase.cn: 气体检测器；瓦斯检查器；检气管
火警探测器；爆炸性气体测定器

deviate.definition: v. turn aside; turn away from\nv. be at variance with; be out of line with\nv. cause to turn away from a previous or expected course
deviate.translation:
vi. 脱离, 偏离
vt. 使偏离
a. 脱离常规的
n. 脱离常规的人

examples.en: Some long lives serve to deviate from the plans of youth.
I don't want to deviate from the plan.
Do not deviate from the standard operating procedure.

devour.definition:
v. destroy completely
v. enjoy avidly
v. eat immoderately
v. eat greedily
devour.translation: vt. 吞食, 挥霍, 吞没

examples.en: He devoured his meal.
examples.zh: 他狼吞虎咽地吃了一顿。

examples.en: Not far away, screened by the forest, crouched Shiegra, the lioness, intent upon devouring the infant for her evening meal.
examples.zh: 不远处，母狮谢格拉匍匐著，隐匿于林间，正伺机将婴儿吞食，作为她的晚餐。

devout.translation: a. 虔诚的, 虔敬的, 诚恳的

examples.en: He's a devout Muslim, and prays in the office.
Tom was a devout Christian who believed in miracles.
Sometimes it's the converts who are the most devout.

dew.definition: n. water that has condensed on a cool surface overnight from water vapor in the air
dew.translation: n. 露珠, 露水\nvt. (用露水)沾湿\nvi. 结露水

examples.en: The dew on the trees sparkles in the morning sun.
Frozen water is called ice; dew congealed is called frost.
Our enemies will vanish like dew in the sun.

words.tran: 带露水的，露湿的；如露的

diameter.definition: n. the length of a straight line passing through the center of a circle and connecting two points on the circumference\nn. a straight line connecting the center of a circle with two points on its perimeter (or the center of a sphere with two points on its surface)
diameter.translation: n. 直径\n[医] 直经, 径

examples.en: Is it possible to determine the diameter from the circumference?
examples.zh: 用圆周能不能求得直径？

words.tran: 直径的；正好相反的；截然的
完全地；作为直径地；直接地；正好相反地

phrase.cn: 粒径；颗粒直径，粒子直径

dictation.definition: n. speech intended for reproduction in writing\nn. matter that has been dictated and transcribed; a dictated passage
dictation.translation: n. 听写, 口述, 命令

examples.en: Have you finished your homework? Have you memorized the dictation content?
examples.zh: 这次作业做完了吗？默写背了吗？

diffuse.definition: v. move outward\ns. spread out; not concentrated in one place\ns. lacking conciseness
diffuse.translation: v. 散播, 传播\na. 散开的, 弥漫的

examples.en: There were no galaxies or even stars, only diffuse gas.
There are focused and diffuse modes of thinking.
A great light was diffused over the baseball stadium.

words.tran: 普及的；散布性的；冗长的
散布，传播（diffuse的过去分词）；使分散

phrase.cn: 漫反射率；漫反射系数；护散反射率

dignified.definition: a. having or expressing dignity; especially formality or stateliness in bearing or appearance\ns. having or showing self-esteem
dignified.translation: a. 有尊严的, 高尚的

examples.en: You look very dignified.
examples.zh: 你看起来很威严。

dime.definition: n. a United States coin worth one tenth of a dollar

examples.en: He who is born for a dime, will never be worth a quarter.
examples.zh: 出生是一分钱，永远不会变成一角钱。

examples.en: You can't seriously expect that they won't recognize you in that disguise. That lopsided, dime store moustache is a dead giveaway!
examples.zh: 你不能指望他们认不出你的伪装。那个歪半边的一角店胡子是致命漏洞！

dire.definition: s fraught with extreme danger; nearly hopeless\ns causing fear or dread or terror
dire.translation: a. 可怕的, 悲惨的, 阴沉的, 极端的

examples.en: I'm in dire need of money.
examples.zh: 我真的很需要钱！

discern.translation: v. 辨别, 看清楚, 了解

examples.en: With adequate lighting, one can easily discern Nosferatu, with his pointed incisors and extremely long-limbed fingers, known as arachnodactyly, from common vampires.
examples.zh: 在光线充足的情况下，诺斯费拉图与普通吸血鬼很容易区分。诺斯费拉图有著尖锐的门牙，以及极为修长的手指，即所谓的蜘蛛指。

words.tran: 有辨识能力的；眼光敏锐的

discharge.definition:
n. the sudden giving off of energy
n. the act of venting
n. a substance that is emitted or released
n. any of several bodily processes by which substances go out of the body
discharge.translation: vt. 卸下, 放出, 解雇, 拔染, 履行, 放电\nvi. 卸货, 流出\nn. 卸货, 流出, 放电

examples.en: The crowd obstructed the police in the discharge of their duties.
examples.zh: 群众妨碍了警员执行任务。

examples.en: The wound discharged pus.
examples.zh: 伤口流出脓液。

phrase.cn: 局部放电；部分放电；部份履行
电火花加工；[电]放电机械制作

disciple.definition: n. someone who believes and helps to spread the doctrine of another

examples.en: After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother and brothers and his disciples.
examples.zh: 这之后他与他的母亲、兄弟和门徒们一起去了迦百农。

disclaimer.definition: n. (law) a voluntary repudiation of a person's legal claim to something
disclaimer.translation: n. 放弃, 拒负责任, 不承诺\n[经] 弃权或不申诉条款

examples.en: Does this need a disclaimer?
examples.zh: 这需要加免责声明吗？

discord.definition: n. lack of agreement or harmony\nn. disagreement among those expected to cooperate\nn. strife resulting from a lack of agreement
discord.translation: n. 不调和, 不和\nvi. 不一致, (声音)刺耳

examples.en: Finally, the discord between them came to an end.
examples.zh: 他们的冲突终于平息了。

examples.en: He sows discord by raising controversial subjects.
examples.zh: 他挑起争议性高的话题，制造纷争。

discretion.definition: n. freedom to act or judge on one's own\nn. knowing how to avoid embarrassment or distress\nn. the trait of judging wisely and objectively
discretion.translation: n. 慎重, 辨别力, 考虑, 处理权\n[法] 有决定权的

examples.en: This plan has discretion advised.
examples.zh: 此计划建议谨慎行事。

disdain.definition:
n lack of respect accompanied by a feeling of intense dislike
n a communication that indicates lack of respect by patronizing the recipient
v look down on with disdain
v reject with contempt
disdain.translation: n. 蔑视\nvt. 蔑视, 鄙弃

examples.en: Tom didn't notice the look of disdain on Mary's face.
It is necessary to have a healthy disdain for wealth.
If you disdain him, the public will blame you.

disgrace.definition:
n a state of dishonor
v bring shame or dishonor upon
v reduce in worth or character, usually verbally
v damage the reputation of
disgrace.translation: n. 耻辱, 不名誉\nvt. 使受耻辱, 使失体面

examples.en: What you did brought disgrace on the whole class.
examples.zh: 你的行为使全班的人丢脸。

examples.en: When the granaries are full, people observe rules of decorum; when food and clothing are sufficient, people understand honor and disgrace.
examples.zh: 粮仓充实了，百姓才会懂得礼仪规矩；衣食丰足了，人们才会知晓荣辱羞耻。

words.tran: 耻辱；贬谪（disgrace的过去式和过去分词）

syno.tran: 耻辱；丢脸的人或事；失宠

disillusion.definition: n freeing from false belief or illusions\nv free from enchantment
disillusion.translation: n. 觉醒, 幻灭\nvt. 使醒悟, 使幻想破灭

examples.en: Disillusion can become itself an illusion if we rest in it.
ATARASHII GAKKO! made new video clips with Captain Disillusion.

dismantle.definition: v tear down so as to make flat with the ground\nv take apart into its constituent pieces\nv take off or remove
dismantle.translation: vt. 拆除...的设备, 分解, 去除覆盖物

examples.en: They will relinquish power and dismantle the single-party state.
Tom dismantled the radio and put it back together again.
The chief said that this faction cannot be considered dismantled.

words.tran: 拆卸；拆除的行动或状态

syno.tran: 拆除；取消；解散；除掉…的覆盖物

dismay.definition: v. fill with apprehension or alarm; cause to be unpleasantly surprised
dismay.translation: n. 沮丧\nvt. 使惊愕, 使气馁

examples.en: Tom gave a cry of dismay.
examples.zh: 汤姆失望地叫了起来。

words.tran: 吃惊，惊愕；心慌；心中不快
使…灰心；使…害怕（dismay的过去式及过去分词）

dispense.definition: v. grant a dispensation; grant an exemption
dispense.translation: vt. 分发, 分配\nvi. 特许, 豁免

examples.en: I can dispense with her help.
examples.zh: 我不需要她的帮助。

disposable.definition: n. an item that can be disposed of after it has been used\na. free or available for use or disposition\na. designed to be disposed of after use
disposable.translation: a. 可任意处理的\n[法] 可任意处理或处置的, 可自由使用的

examples.en: In this society where everything is disposable, it is a virtue to use something until it wears out.
examples.zh: 在这个社会里一切都是用完即丢, 用东西直到它磨损是一种美德。

words.tran: 有…倾向的；打算做…的；有某种健康状态的
处置；[心理] 性情；[军] 部署；倾向
处理；配置；使适应（dispose的过去分词）；使有倾向

disproportionate.definition: a. out of proportion\ns. not proportionate

examples.en: There is a disproportionate number of girls in the class.
This big gate is disproportionate to the small garden.
The disproportionate power of the Western world has started to decline.

disseminate.definition: v cause to become widely known
disseminate.translation: vt. 散播, 传播, 宣传\nvi. 广为传播

examples.en: If you're going to disseminate ideas, make sure they're worthwhile.
Disseminating knowledge is not the mission of the website.
Lukas disseminated Rima’s nude pictures over the Internet.

dissipate.definition: v. live a life of pleasure, especially with respect to alcoholic consumption
dissipate.translation: vt. 散失, 驱散, 浪费\nvi. 消散, 放荡

examples.en: Let's not dissipate our efforts on pointless and time-wasting schemes.
The fog started to dissipate about ten o'clock.
When I really got to know her, the magic dissipated.

words.tran: 消散的；沉迷于酒色的；闲游浪荡的；放荡的

dissolution.definition: n. separation into component parts\nn. the termination or disintegration of a relationship (between persons or nations)
dissolution.translation: n. 分解, 溶解, 解散, 结束\n[化] 溶解; 溶解作用

examples.en: Tom and Mary announced the dissolution of their marriage.
Justice without mercy is cruelty; mercy without justice is the mother of dissolution.
The predominant belief since the dissolution of the Soviet Union has been that another world is not possible.

distill.definition: v. undergo the process of distillation\nv. extract by the process of distillation\nv. give off (a liquid)

examples.en: Old Man Tom is a great master at distilling moonshine.
This distillery uses organic grains and distills its whiskey from scratch.
Now we will distill this water.

words.tran: 蒸馏，净化；蒸馏法；精华，蒸馏物
蒸馏；蒸馏物；蒸馏法；精华（等于distilment或者distillation）
蒸馏；提取…的精华；使渗出

syno.tran: 蒸馏；滴下；作为精华产生（等于distil）

diverge.definition: v. move or draw apart\nv. have no limits as a mathematical series\nv. extend in a different direction
diverge.translation: vi. 分歧, 岔开\nvt. 使岔开

examples.en: On the best time to drink this wine, opinions diverge.
The roads diverge up ahead; take the left one.
Berber and Semitic languages diverged from each other several thousands of years ago.

words.tran: 发散的；分歧的；岔开的（等于divergent）
分歧；分叉；意见不同；分支

dodgy.definition: s of uncertain outcome; especially fraught with risk\ns marked by skill in deception
dodgy.translation: a. 狡猾的, 逃避的, 难弄的

examples.en: The used car salesman seemed a bit dodgy to me.
He accompanies his songs with sad chords played on a dodgy zither.
That website seems a bit dodgy, I wouldn't enter your credit card information there.

dome.definition: n. a concave shape whose distinguishing characteristic is that the concavity faces downward\nn. a stadium that has a roof\nn. a hemispherical roof
dome.translation: n. 圆顶\nvt. 加圆顶\nvi. 成圆顶状

examples.en: What's the number for the Tokyo Dome?
examples.zh: 东京巨蛋的电话号码是多少？

words.tran: 凸起；[矿业] 成拱作用
在…上加穹顶；隆起成穹顶状（dome的过去分词）

phrase.cn: 穹状构造；穹隆构造；穹窿构造

dormant.definition: s. in a condition of biological rest or suspended animation\na. (of e.g. volcanos) not erupting and not extinct\ns. lying with head on paws as if sleeping
dormant.translation: a. 睡眠状态的, 静止的\n[医] 休眠的, 不活动的, 休止的

examples.en: Mt. Asama is now dormant.
examples.zh: 浅间山现在是寂静的。

dormitory.definition: n. a college or university building containing living quarters for students\nn. a large sleeping room containing several beds

examples.en: We will all be playing in the dormitory tomorrow night, can you come?
examples.zh: 明天晚上我们都去宿舍玩儿，你能不能去？

examples.en: The university has classrooms as well as dormitories.
examples.zh: 大学有教室，也有宿舍。

examples.en: I left the notes in the dormitory. I'll go back and get them now.
examples.zh: 我把笔记放在宿舍了，现在回去拿。

dosage.definition: n the quantity of an active agent (substance or radiation) taken in or absorbed at any one time\nn a measured portion of medicine taken at any one time
dosage.translation: n. 剂量, 用量, 配药\n[医] 剂量

examples.en: If the medicine isn't working, maybe we should up the dosage.
What is the maximum dosage for an adult?
The dosage last night was much higher.

dough.definition: n. a flour mixture stiff enough to knead or roll
dough.translation: n. 生面团\n[化] 捏塑体; 生面团

examples.en: Add water and mix to a firm dough.
examples.zh: 加水，和成一个结实的面团。

examples.en: Roll the dough into a rectangle.
examples.zh: 把面团擀成方形。

examples.en: Hand over the dough!
examples.zh: 把钱交出来！

dove.definition: n. any of numerous small pigeons\nn. someone who prefers negotiations to armed conflict in the conduct of foreign relations\nn. an emblem of peace

examples.en: There is a white dove on the roof.
examples.zh: 屋顶上有只白鸽。

examples.en: A white dove is on the roof.
examples.zh: 屋顶上有只白鸽。

examples.en: There's a white dove on the roof.
examples.zh: 屋顶上有只白鸽。

words.tran: 潜水者；跳水的选手；潜鸟
潜水；跳水；俯冲；急剧下降

downfall.definition: n. failure that results in a loss of position or reputation

examples.en: Arrogance leads to a person's downfall.
examples.zh: 骄傲使人落后。

downside.definition: n. a negative aspect of something that is generally positive

examples.en: Certainly there are downsides to leadership by coercion and force.
A downside to frequent flyer miles is that using them is complicated.
Hatred is the downside of being cute.

downtown.definition: a. of or located in the lower part of a town, or in the business center\nr. toward or in the lower or central part of town
downtown.translation: n. 市中心区\na. 市中心的\nadv. 往闹市区

examples.en: The downtown area is the heart of the city.
examples.zh: 市中心是城市之心。

examples.en: Let's have lunch downtown and take in a show.
examples.zh: 我们去市区吃饭，然后再看场电影吧。

examples.en: The house I bought is pretty far from downtown.
examples.zh: 我买的房子离市中心比较远。

downturn.definition: n. a worsening of business or economic activity
downturn.translation: n. (尤指经济方面的)衰退, 下降趋势\n[电] 低迷时期

examples.en: The best companies are usually investing during an economic downturn.
Will the global economy face another downturn?
Can the economy handle another downturn?

doze.translation: vi. 打瞌睡, 假寐\nvt. 打瞌睡度过\nn. 瞌睡

examples.zh: 门口有个人。

daisy.definition: n. any of numerous composite plants having flower heads with well-developed ray flowers usually arranged in a single whorl
daisy.translation: n. 雏菊, 一流人物\na. 第一流的

examples.en: A little nap and, just like that, I'm as fresh as a daisy.
examples.zh: 我小睡后就感到生龙活虎。

examples.en: There are daisies next to the steel building.
examples.zh: 在钢铁大厦的旁边有许多的雏菊。

examples.en: There are daisies around the steel building.
examples.zh: 那里有许多雏菊围绕着钢铁大厦。

defendant.definition: n. a person or institution against whom an action is brought in a court of law; the person being sued or accused
defendant.translation: n. 被告\n[经] 被告方

examples.en: The defendant will appeal to a higher court.
examples.zh: 被告会向上级法院上诉。

examples.en: The court declared the defendant innocent.
examples.zh: 法庭宣判被告无罪。

examples.en: The news article painted the defendant as a guilty man, even though he had been proven innocent.
examples.zh: 该报文章中将被告人描述成一个罪魁祸首，尽管他已经被证明是无辜的了。

words.tran: 可防御的；可辩护的；可拥护的
防卫者，守卫者；辩护者；拥护者；卫冕者

donkey.definition: n. the symbol of the Democratic Party; introduced in cartoons by Thomas Nast in 1874
donkey.translation: n. 驴子, 笨蛋, 顽固者, 辅助发动机, 辅助泵

examples.en: That's not a horse, it's a donkey.
examples.zh: 那不是只马，是只驴子。

examples.en: Jessie urged the little donkey forward.
examples.zh: 杰西鞭策小毛驴前进。

examples.en: I have a donkey.
examples.zh: 我有一头驴。

diamond.definition: n. a transparent piece of diamond that has been cut and polished and is valued as a precious gem\nn. very hard native crystalline carbon valued as a gem\nn. a playing card in the minor suit that has one or more red rhombuses on it
diamond.translation: n. 钻石, 菱形\n[计] 菱形

examples.en: The diamond was set in a gold ring.
examples.zh: 钻石被镶在一个金戒指上。

examples.en: This diamond ring is too extravagant for me.
examples.zh: 我觉得这钻石戒指太奢侈了。

examples.en: This may not be a real diamond.
examples.zh: 这可能不是一颗真的钻石。

syno.tran: [宝]钻石，[矿物]金刚石；[数]菱形；方块牌

dragon.definition: n. a creature of Teutonic mythology; usually represented as breathing fire and having a reptilian body and sometimes wings\nn. a fiercely vigilant and unpleasant woman\nn. any of several small tropical Asian lizards capable of gliding by spreading winglike membranes on each side of the body
dragon.translation: n. 龙, 凶暴的人\n[法] 凶恶的人, 凶恶严厉的监护人

examples.en: The dragon is one of the cultural emblems of China.
examples.zh: 龙是中国的文化图腾。

examples.en: "Drawing dragons and dotting in the eyes" is a fable.
examples.zh: 画龙点睛是一则寓言故事。

examples.en: The book tells the story of a dragon that can't breathe fire.
examples.zh: 书里讲的是一条不会喷火的龙的故事。

syno.tran: 龙；凶暴的人，凶恶的人；严厉而有警觉性的女人

drum.definition:
n. a musical percussion instrument; usually consists of a hollow cylinder with a membrane stretched across each end
n. the sound of a drum
n. a cylindrical metal container used for shipping or storage of liquids
n. small to medium-sized bottom-dwelling food and game fishes of shallow coastal and fresh waters that make a drumming noise
drum.translation:
n. 鼓, 鼓声
vi. 击鼓, 作鼓声
vt. 打鼓奏出
[计] 磁鼓

examples.en: I sent this drum to my father.
examples.zh: 我送了个长鼓给我父亲。

examples.en: Jim likes to play the drum.
examples.zh: 吉姆喜欢打鼓。

examples.en: She can play the drum.
examples.zh: 她会打鼓。

phrase.cn: 招徕（顾客）；[口]竭力争取；纠集；鼓动
锅炉汽包，锅筒；鼓筒式锅炉

daring.definition:
n a challenge to do something dangerous or foolhardy
n the trait of being willing to undertake things that involve risk or danger
v take upon oneself; act presumptuously, without permission
v to be courageous enough to try or do something
v challenge
s disposed to venture or take risks
s radically new or original

examples.en: The daring expedition to the North Pole was a success.
Tom was punished for daring to break the unwritten law.
It was a daring adventure, full of thrill and excitement.

dart.definition:
n. a small narrow pointed missile that is thrown or shot
n. a tapered tuck made in dressmaking
v. run or move very quickly or hastily
v. move with sudden speed
dart.translation: n. 飞镖, 投射\nvt. 投射\nvi. 疾走, 突进

examples.en: The last dart he threw, bounced off the board.
Tom was killed by a poison dart fired from a blowgun.
The tiger was hit with a tranquilizer dart.

deadlock.definition: n. a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible
deadlock.translation: n. 僵局, 停顿\nv. (使)停顿, (使)相持不下\n[计] 死锁

examples.en: We must try to break the deadlock.
examples.zh: 我们必须设法打破这个僵局。

deceit.definition: n the quality of being fraudulent\nn a misleading falsehood\nn the act of deceiving
deceit.translation: n. 欺骗, 谎言\n[经] 诈骗, 欺骗

examples.en: He acquired a great fortune by using deceit and treachery.
Lying, or deceit, represents a violation of basic Zoroastrian beliefs.
Fraud and deceit abound in these days more than in former times.

words.tran: 欺骗的；欺诈的；谎言的；虚伪的

deceptive.definition: s. causing one to believe what is not true or fail to believe what is true\ns. designed to deceive or mislead either deliberately or inadvertently
deceptive.translation: a. 迷惑的, 虚伪的, 欺诈的

examples.en: Looks can be deceptive.
examples.zh: 外表可以骗人。

declarative.definition: a. relating to the use of or having the nature of a declaration
declarative.translation: a. 宣言的, 陈述的, 说明的, 公告的\n[计] 说明的

examples.en: You must put a period at the end of each declarative sentence.
This is not a declarative sentence!
This is a simple declarative sentence.

defection.definition: n withdrawing support or help despite allegiance or responsibility\nn the state of having rejected your religious beliefs or your political party or a cause (often in favor of opposing beliefs or causes)
defection.translation: n. 背叛, 缺乏, 毛病\n[法] 缺点, 过失, 背叛

examples.en: My government continues to treat dissent as defection.

deletion.definition: n. (genetics) the loss or absence of one or more nucleotides from a chromosome\nn. the omission that is made when an editorial change shortens a written passage\nn. the act of deleting something written or printed
deletion.translation: n. 删除, 删除部分\n[医] 缺失, 中间缺失(染色体)

examples.en: It is highly probable that the deletion of element C will still yield the same result.
examples.zh: 很有可能去掉C元素会得出同样的结果。

delude.definition: v be false to; be dishonest with

examples.en: Oh! I'm not deluding myself!
examples.zh: 啊！我没有骗自己！

demanding.definition: a. requiring more than usually expected or thought due; especially great patience and effort and skill
demanding.translation: a. 要求高的, 费力的

examples.en: Kate broke his heart by rudely demanding he go away.
The scores are low because the task is cognitively demanding.
Algerian Islamists are demanding a state founded on Islamic law.

denunciation.definition: n. a public act of denouncing
denunciation.translation: n. 谴责, 告发\n[经] 废止合同(契约), 宣告合同(契约等)无效

examples.en: The world must unite in the denunciation of colonial practices.
Citizens lived in constant fear of denunciation and repression.
Denunciation and sanctions are vital steps toward a more just world.

depiction.definition: n. representation by drawing or painting etc

examples.en: I think I am the depiction of God under his human form.
The movie is a harrowing depiction of life in an urban slum.
Dickens' thoughts come across along with the vivid depiction of old London.

depletion.definition: n. the act of decreasing something markedly\nn. the state of being depleted
depletion.translation: n. 消耗, 耗尽, 放血\n[医] 排除, 缺失(液体), 衰竭[状态](由于缺液)

examples.en: The best refutation of the imaginary Malthusian laws of "land depletion" is the practice of Soviet collective farming.
examples.zh: 对马尔萨斯虚构的「土地耗尽」定律最有力的反驳，是苏联集体农场的时间。

deplore.definition: v. express strong disapproval of\nv. regret strongly
deplore.translation: vt. 悲悼, 哀叹, 对...深感遗憾

examples.en: He deplored the fact that Silesia was no longer Prussian.
One must deplore such bad behavior.
We deplore your cruelty to animals.

deport.definition: v behave in a certain manner\nv hand over to the authorities of another country\nv expel from a country
deport.translation: vt. 举止, 驱逐出境\n[法] 放逐, 驱逐, 递解

examples.en: Tom and Mary were afraid that they might be deported.
Tom and Mary hope that they won't be deported.
Do you really think that Tom will be deported?

deportation.definition: n. the expulsion from a country of an undesirable alien
deportation.translation: n. 驱逐出境, 放逐\n[法] 递解出境, 放逐, 驱逐

examples.en: It is unlikely that this indictment will lead to his deportation.
Sami faced deportation back to his native Egypt.
Layla faced deportation back to her native Egypt.

derail.definition: v. cause to run off the tracks\nv. run off or leave the rails
derail.translation: vt. 使出轨\nn. 脱轨器\n[计] 转移指令

examples.en: I had a close call when my car derailed.
A freight train has derailed just south of Stockholm.
He was traveling in that train which derailed.

derailment.definition: n. an accident in which a train runs off its track

examples.en: The suspected cause of the derailment is a landslide.
The train was traveling from Aberdeen to Glasgow when the derailment occurred.
What caused the train derailment?
Does Algeria need to deregulate its markets?
Algeria needs to deregulate its economy.
We must deregulate the economy.

deregulation.definition: n. the act of freeing from regulation (especially from governmental regulations)
deregulation.translation: n. 撤消(价格等的)管制规定, 解除控制

examples.en: It is difficult to peg the direction of interest deregulation.
Therefore, they cannot catalyze deregulation without "external pressure".
Gas is a little cheaper with self-service, now that deregulation is kicking in.

derivative.definition: n. a compound obtained from, or regarded as derived from, another compound\nn. (linguistics) a word that is derived from another word\ns. resulting from or employing derivation
derivative.translation: a. 引出的, 派生的\nn. 引出之物, 派生物, 衍生字

examples.en: I can take the integral and the derivative. And you?
The derivative of a constant function is always zero.
Copyright owners have the right to control derivative works.

descriptive.definition: a. serving to describe or inform or characterized by description\na. describing the structure of a language
descriptive.translation: a. 描述的, 叙述的

examples.en: In Korean, adjectives often function as descriptive verbs, meaning they can be conjugated like verbs to express different tenses and moods.
examples.zh: 在韩语中，形容词通常充当描述性动词，这意味著它们可以像动词一样变位以表达不同的时态和语气。

desertion.definition: n. withdrawing support or help despite allegiance or responsibility
desertion.translation: n. 丢掉, 遗弃, 逃亡\n[法] 长期分居, 开小差, 遗弃

examples.en: Desertion from the army was grounds for the death penalty.
Desertion from the army was punishable by death.
Twenty six soldiers were executed for desertion.

desirability.definition: n. the quality of being worthy of desiring
desirability.translation: n. 值得想望, 可取\n[经] 合意性, 可用性

examples.en: I'm starting to question my worth and desirability.
Scads of online daters constantly check their desirability.
Western media and popular culture often depict Western lifestyles and ideals as the epitome of success and desirability.

destined.definition:
v decree or designate beforehand
v design or destine
s headed or intending to head in a certain direction; often used as a combining form as in `college-bound students'
s (usually followed by `to') governed by fate
destined.translation: a. 预定的, 注定的, 命定的

examples.en: He was destined to become a great musician.
examples.zh: 他命中注定要成为伟大的音乐家。

detached.definition:
s. being or feeling set or kept apart from others
s. no longer connected or joined
a. used of buildings; standing apart from others
s. lacking affection or warm feeling
detached.translation: a. 超然的, 分离的, 冷淡的\n[法] 分遣的, 派遣的, 分离的

examples.en: The beautiful red leaves of the maple become detached from the branches and are dancing in the wind.
examples.zh: 枫树美丽的红叶从枝头飘落，在风中翩翩起舞。

detriment.translation: n. 损害, 损害物\n[法] 损害, 伤害, 危害

examples.en: How quickly to my detriment cruel Luck has changed!
The poor educational policy is a detriment to Japan.
This discovery has been exploited to the detriment of the poor peasants.

devastating.definition:
v cause extensive destruction or ruin utterly
v overwhelm or overpower
s making light of
s wreaking or capable of wreaking complete destruction
s physically or spiritually devastating; often used in combination
devastating.translation: a. 毁灭性的, (非正式)很好的, 引人注目的

examples.en: A devastating earthquake hit the state capital.
examples.zh: 一场毁灭性的地震袭击了这个州的首府。

diffusion.definition: n. (physics) the process in which there is movement of a substance from an area of high concentration of that substance to an area of lower concentration\nn. the spread of social institutions (and myths and skills) from one society to another
diffusion.translation: n. 散播, 传播, 蔓延\n[医] 扩散, 弥散, 漫射(光)

examples.en: Diffusion is passive because it doesn't require an external source of energy.

digestion.definition: n. the process of decomposing organic matter (as in sewage) by bacteria or by chemical action or heat\nn. the organic process by which food is converted into substances that can be absorbed into the body\nn. learning and coming to understand ideas and information
digestion.translation: n. 消化力, 领悟\n[化] 消化; 消化作用; 蒸煮; 蒸煮作用; 煮解; 浸提; 陈化

examples.en: Don't eat too much and disrupt the stomach's normal digestion process.
examples.zh: 不要因为吃得太多而扰乱胃的正常消化。

examples.en: Wine helps with digestion.
examples.zh: 葡萄酒帮助消化。

examples.en: Drinking wine aids digestion.
examples.zh: 喝酒帮助消化。

digit.definition: n. one of the elements that collectively form a system of numeration\nn. a finger or toe in human beings or corresponding body part in other vertebrates
digit.translation: n. 数字, 位数, 指头\n[计] 数位; 位

examples.en: Hey, give me your digits. I will tell you about the seaside and the stars.
examples.zh: 嘿，把你的电话号码给我。我会跟你讲讲海边和星星的故事。

dignify.translation: vt. 增威严, 使高贵, 故作显贵

examples.en: I'm not even going to dignify that with an answer.
Such a statement I would not dignify with a response.
I refuse to dignify that with a response.

diligence.definition: n. conscientiousness in paying proper attention to a task; giving the degree of care required in a given situation\nn. persevering determination to perform a task

examples.en: Her diligence is a good example to us all.
examples.zh: 她的用功对我们所有人是一个好的榜样。

dilution.definition: n. a diluted solution\nn. weakening (reducing the concentration) by the addition of water or a thinner
dilution.translation: n. 冲淡, 淡度, 稀度, 稀释物, 冲淡物, 稀释\n[计] 稀释度的

examples.en: The stock got creamed when they got wind of the dilution.
Our chemistry lesson yesterday was about dilution of acids and bases.
Without water, pharmaceutical preparations and dilutions can't be made.

diner.definition: n. a person eating a meal (especially in a restaurant)\nn. a restaurant that resembles a dining car

examples.en: Tom told me you ate at Chuck's Diner last night.
I know that you'll enjoy the food at Chuck's Diner.
It was fun going to Chuck's Diner with you.

diplomacy.translation: n. 外交, 外交手腕, 交际手段\n[法] 外交, 外交手腕, 权谋

examples.en: International problems must be solved by diplomacy, not war.
examples.zh: 国际问题必须靠外交而非战争解决。

examples.en: English is useful in diplomacy and tourism.
examples.zh: 英语在外交和旅游业方面很有用。

disable.definition: v. make unable to perform a certain action\nv. injure permanently
disable.translation: vt. 使失去能力, 使残废, (律)使无资格\n[计] 使无效, 禁止, 关闭

examples.en: I wish I could figure out how to disable comments on my blog.
examples.zh: 但愿我能找到在我的博客上屏蔽评论的办法。

words.tran: 使…失去能力（disable的过去分词）

syno.tran: 使失去能力；使残废；使无资格

disappointing.translation: a. 使失望的, 期待落空的, 令人沮丧的

examples.en: I am sorry for disappointing you.
examples.zh: 对不起，是我辜负你了。

examples.en: You are a disappointing person!
examples.zh: 你这种人差劲吗！

examples.en: The speaker didn't know his subject, nor did he speak well; in short, he was disappointing.
examples.zh: 演讲者不熟悉他的主题，说得又不好，总之，他很糟糕。

disapproval.definition: n. a feeling of disliking something or what someone is doing\nn. the expression of disapproval\nn. the act of disapproving or condemning

examples.en: Continuing to eat while I talk will only intensify my disapproval.
He showed his disapproval by raising an eyebrow.
They communicate disapproval by shaking their heads.

words.tran: 不以为然地；非难地；不赞成地

disapprove.definition: v. consider bad or wrong\nv. deem wrong or inappropriate

examples.en: Some people disapprove of the education system in the Netherlands.
I can tell from your expression that you disapprove.
Do you approve or disapprove of my project?

disarm.definition: v. remove offensive capability from\nv. make less hostile; win over\nv. take away the weapons from; render harmless
disarm.translation: vt. 解除武装, 裁军, 缓和\nvi. 放下武器

examples.en: "Your humility, Mr. Bingley," said Elizabeth, "must disarm reproof."
Tom gave Mary what he hoped was a disarming smile.
How are you going to disarm Tom?

disarmament.definition: n act of reducing or depriving of arms
disarmament.translation: n. 裁军\n[法] 裁军, 解除军备

examples.en: The Malian government will organize a disarmament of the MNLA.
A radical disarmament treaty prohibits all armaments and armed forces.
Disarmament is in practice difficult in many countries.

disciplined.definition: s. obeying the rules\ns. trained mentally or physically by instruction or exercise
disciplined.translation: a. 遵守纪律的；受过训练的

examples.en: He didn't meet the obligations and was disciplined for that.
We should learn to be disciplined in our lives.
I wish I'd been more disciplined in my studies.

discourage.definition: v. deprive of courage or hope; take away hope from; cause to feel discouraged

examples.en: He won't be easily discouraged, because he's a tough guy.
examples.zh: 他很坚强，不会那么容易灰心。

examples.en: I didn't mean to discourage you.
examples.zh: 我不想打击你的。

examples.en: Mary told me she wasn't discouraged.
examples.zh: 玛丽告诉我她不气馁。

words.tran: 使人沮丧的；令人气馁的
使人气馁地，使人沮丧地；阻止地
劝阻（discourage的过去分词）；使失去勇气

discreet.definition: a. marked by prudence or modesty and wise self-restraint
discreet.translation: a. 小心的, 慎重的

examples.en: Mary told me that she thought Tom would be discreet.
examples.zh: 玛丽跟我说他觉得汤姆很谨慎。

discriminate.definition:
v. recognize or perceive the difference
v. treat differently on the basis of sex or race
v. distinguish
a. marked by the ability to see or make fine distinctions
discriminate.translation: v. 区别, 差别待遇

examples.en: Discriminating against people because of their race is a mistake.
examples.zh: 因为人的种族而歧视他们是一种错误。

words.tran: 有辨识力的；差别对待的
识别的；有差别的；有识别力的
区别的，歧视的；有识别力的

discriminatory.definition: s. containing or implying a slight or showing prejudice\ns. manifesting partiality
discriminatory.translation: a. 有辨识力的, 有差别的

examples.en: Rodrigo encountered bias and discriminatory behavior on the website.
The English teacher made discriminatory remarks about the foreign students' backgrounds.
Rodrigo faced discriminatory comments and insults from other users on the website.

disgust.definition: n. strong feelings of dislike\nv. fill with distaste\nv. cause aversion in; offend the moral sense of
disgust.translation: n. 厌恶, 嫌恶\nvi. 令人厌恶\nvt. 使作呕

examples.en: I didn't mean to disgust anyone.
examples.zh: 我没想让人感到不适。

examples.en: Sami the picture and he was immediately disgusted.
examples.zh: 萨米看到照片，立刻感到厌恶。

examples.en: I am disgusted with him.
examples.zh: 我厌恶他。

words.tran: 使恶心；使讨厌（disgust的过去分词）

disgusting.definition: s. highly offensive; arousing aversion or disgust

examples.en: My roommate is so disgusting.
examples.zh: 我的室友真恶心。

examples.en: Don't be so disgusting.
examples.zh: 不要这么恶心。

dish.definition:
n. a piece of dishware normally used as a container for holding or serving food
n. a particular item of prepared food
n. the quantity that a dish will hold
n. directional antenna consisting of a parabolic reflector for microwave or radio frequency radiation
dish.translation: n. 盘子, 碟, 菜肴\n[医] 皿, 碟

examples.en: Every time he comes here, he orders the same dish.
examples.zh: 每次他来这里点一样的菜。

examples.en: Nothing is so tasty as the dish you make.
examples.zh: 没有甚么比你做的菜更好吃了。

examples.en: This dish has a bit of garlic flavor.
examples.zh: 这道菜里有点大蒜的味道。

phrase.cn: 起锅，分盛；把食物装盘，盛在盘中端上

disintegrate.definition: v. break into parts or components or lose cohesion or unity\nv. cause to undergo fission or lose particles\nv. lose a stored charge, magnetic flux, or current
disintegrate.translation: vt. (使)分解, (使)碎裂\n[医] 分解, 分裂, 蜕变

examples.en: Another step forward revealed that the skull had received violent impact and disintegrated.
examples.zh: 进一步的检查发现头骨受到剧烈的撞击而碎裂。

disintegration.definition: n. a loss (or serious disruption) of organization in some system
disintegration.translation: n. 瓦解\n[化] 破碎; 崩解; 蜕变

examples.en: Some think that disintegration is unavoidable in Algeria.
Disintegration is quite painless, I assure you.
I have no respect for a person who calls for the disintegration of our beloved Algeria.

words.tran: 使分解；使碎裂；使崩溃；使衰变

dislike.definition: n. a feeling of aversion or antipathy\nv. have or feel a dislike or distaste for
dislike.translation: n. 嫌恶\nvt. 讨厌, 不喜欢

examples.en: I don't like teachers who dislike students that ask questions.
examples.zh: 我讨厌不喜欢学生问问题的老师。

examples.en: To be honest, I've gradually come to dislike the life here.
examples.zh: 老实说, 我已经渐渐地不喜欢这里的生活。

examples.en: The only time people dislike gossip is when you gossip about them.
examples.zh: 人们不喜欢流言蜚语的唯一时间是当你闲聊他们的事。

disregard.definition: n. lack of attention and due care\nn. willful lack of care and attention
disregard.translation: n. 忽视, 漠视\nvt. 忽视, 不顾

examples.en: Disregarding the "No Entry" sign, she pushed open the door and walked inside.
examples.zh: 无视于" 禁止进入" 的牌子，她推开了门走进去。

examples.en: He disregarded his father's advice.
examples.zh: 他不顾他父亲的忠告。

examples.en: He disregarded my advice.
examples.zh: 他不顾我的忠告。

disruption.definition: n. the act of causing disorder
disruption.translation: n. 分裂, 崩溃, 瓦解

examples.en: The accident at the junction caused disruption to traffic flow.
I was very upset by the disruption in my normal morning routine.
The world economy is undergoing constant disruption.

dissident.definition: s. characterized by departure from accepted beliefs or standards
dissident.translation: a. 意见不同的, 持不同政见的\nn. 意见不同的人, 持不同政见者

examples.en: The political dissident has spent nearly a decade under house arrest.
"Dissidents must be tolerated!" "Even when they aren't tolerant themselves?"
All political dissidents were purged under the former regime.

distil.definition:
v undergo condensation; change from a gaseous to a liquid state and fall in drops
v extract by the process of distillation
v undergo the process of distillation
v give off (a liquid)
distil.translation: vt.vi. 蒸馏, 提取...的精华, 用蒸馏法提取\nvi. 滴下, 渗出

examples.en: You can distil water and whiskey.

distraction.definition: n. mental turmoil\nn. an obstacle to attention\nn. the act of distracting; drawing someone's attention away from something
distraction.translation: n. 娱乐, 分心的事物, 分心\n[医] 注意力分散, 内脱位, 牙弓过宽

examples.en: Focus on the goal. Everything else is a distraction.
He took advantage of my moment of distraction to run away.
Sports are supposed to be a distraction from more serious things.

words.tran: 心烦意乱的；思想不集中的

syno.tran: 注意力分散；消遣；心烦意乱

dive.definition:
n. a headlong plunge into water
n. a steep nose-down descent by an aircraft
v. drop steeply
v. plunge into water
dive.translation: n. 潜水, 跳水\nvi. 跳水, 俯冲, 猛冲\nvt. 把...突然伸入

examples.en: He dived into the water and came up for air.
examples.zh: 他潜进水里，然后又浮上水来换气。

examples.en: The goalkeeper for France dived to the ground and saved Ronaldo’s shot.
examples.zh: 法国队守门员扑到地上截住了罗纳尔多的射门。

examples.en: Ken stands on the diving board.
examples.zh: 肯站在跳水台上

words.tran: 潜水者；跳水的选手；潜鸟

syno.tran: [水运]潜水；跳水；[航]俯冲；急剧下降

phrase.cn: v. 投入；把手伸入；钻研
开始大吃；头朝下跳入水中
◎突然下降，急剧下降，(行市等)暴跌

diversify.definition: v. make (more) diverse\nv. spread into new habitats and produce variety or variegate\nv. vary in order to spread risk or to expand
diversify.translation: vt. 使多样化, 使变化

examples.en: Gold is not a good way to diversify your money.
The best thing Algeria could do is diversify its economy.
Algeria is trying extremely hard to diversify its revenue base.

divisive.definition: s dissenting (especially dissenting with the majority opinion)
divisive.translation: a. 区分的, 制造分裂的, 造成不和的

examples.en: It was never my intent to be divisive or polarizing.
Use of such divisive language tends to polarize the public.
The war in Ukraine has been a divisive debate in Europe.

doctoral.definition: a. of or relating to a doctor or doctorate

examples.en: Even if she wasn't sick, she couldn't complete her doctoral thesis by the deadline because the thesis problem contains a vast amount of detail.
examples.zh: 即使她没生病，到了规定的日期她也完成不了她的博士论文， 因为论文题目涉及的内容太广泛。

words.tran: 修理；窜改，伪造；为…治病；授以博士学位

doctorate.definition: n one of the highest earned academic degrees conferred by a university

examples.en: She received a doctorate.
examples.zh: 她取得了博士学位。

dodge.definition:
n. a quick evasive movement
n. a statement that evades the question by cleverness or trickery
v. make a sudden movement in a new direction so as to avoid
v. move to and fro or from place to place usually in an irregular course
dodge.translation: v. 避开, 躲避\nn. 诡计, 躲藏

examples.en: Don't dodge the issue, I want you to answer my question.
examples.zh: 不要逃避，我要你回答我的问题。

words.tran: 狡猾的，逃避的；善于骗人的；躲闪的

dogma.definition: n. a religious doctrine that is proclaimed as true without proof\nn. a doctrine or code of beliefs accepted as authoritative

examples.en: His dogma forbids that he eats fish during Passover.
God is an uncontested dogma in many religions.
I don't agree with the interpretation of many Christian dogmas.

dole.definition: n. a share of money or food or clothing that has been charitably given\nn. money received from the state
dole.translation: n. 救济品, 失业救济金\nvt. 发放救济

examples.en: Tom has been on the dole since the 6th of August when he lost his job.
examples.zh: Tom从八月六号他失业那天，开始领失业救济金。

syno.tran: [劳经]失业救济金；赈济物；施舍品

downgrade.definition: n. the property possessed by a slope or surface that descends\nv. rate lower; lower in value or esteem
downgrade.translation:
vt. 降低, 贬低
n. 下坡
a. 下坡
adv. 下坡

examples.en: You call that an upgrade? It's more of a downgrade, if you ask me.
Until the bug is resolved, I advise you to downgrade your video card drivers.
Going from Starbucks to instant coffee is a massive downgrade, if you ask me.

dropout.definition: n. someone who quits school before graduation\nn. someone who withdraws from a social group or environment
dropout.translation: n. 退学学生, 中途退学\n[电] 离去

examples.en: I know that Tom is a high school dropout.
Sami is a high-school dropout without a real job.
I know Tom is a high school dropout.

drunkard.translation: n. 酒鬼\n[医] 嗜酒者

examples.en: He's a drunkard.
examples.zh: 他是个酒鬼。

drunken.definition: s given to or marked by the consumption of alcohol

examples.en: A drunken man was sleeping on the bench.
examples.zh: 一个醉了的男人在长椅上睡觉。

examples.en: The policeman arrested him for drunken driving.
examples.zh: 警察因酒后驾驶逮捕了他。

examples.en: He was arrested for drunken driving.
examples.zh: 他因酒后驾驶而被捕。

duly.translation: adv. 恰当地, 充分地, 适当地, 及时地

examples.en: Candidates must be duly nominated by the electoral commission.
He's been duly appointed as the assistant director of the program.
They are now man and wife duly married.

durability.definition: n permanence by virtue of the power to resist stress or force
durability.translation: [计] 耐久性, 耐用性, 持久性

examples.en: He checked the durability of the house before buying it.
This machine is inferior to that one in durability.
Support during tough times tests love's durability.

dentist.definition: n. a person qualified to practice dentistry
dentist.translation: n. 牙科医生\n[医] 牙医师

examples.en: A trip to the dentist feels like it'll kill me.
examples.zh: 看牙医真的会要了我的老命。

examples.en: It's best to go to the dentist at regular intervals.
examples.zh: 最好定期去看牙医。

examples.en: How often do you have to see the dentist?
examples.zh: 你多久看一次牙医？

words.tran: 齿列；生齿；[脊椎] 齿系

diary.definition: n. a daily written record of (usually personal) experiences and observations\nn. a personal journal (as a physical object)
diary.translation: n. 日记\n[经] 日记簿

examples.en: By the way, how many of you keep a diary?
examples.zh: 对了，你们当中写日记的有几位？

examples.en: I have decided to keep a diary this year.
examples.zh: 这一年我下了决心写日记。

examples.en: Who was it that read my diary while I was out?
examples.zh: 是谁趁我不在的时候看我的日记？

dirt.definition: n. the state of being covered with unclean things\ns. (of roads) not leveled or drained; unsuitable for all year travel
dirt.translation: n. 污垢, 泥土\n[化] 污垢

examples.en: Tom is washing the dirt off the plates.
examples.zh: Tom洗去盘子上的污垢。

examples.en: Tom likes to play in the dirt.
examples.zh: 汤姆喜欢在污垢里玩。

examples.en: You can dig dirt from the ground.
examples.zh: 你可以在地上挖土。

words.tran: 下流的，卑鄙的；污秽的；恶劣的；暗淡的

syno.tran: 污垢，泥土；灰尘，尘土；下流话

doctor.definition:
n. a licensed medical practitioner
n. children take the roles of physician or patient or nurse and pretend they are at the physician's office
n. a person who holds Ph.D. degree (or the equivalent) from an academic institution
v. give medical treatment to
doctor.translation: n. 医生, 博士\nvt. 授以博士学位, 诊断, 修改\nvi. 行医

examples.en: I aim to be a doctor when I grow up.
examples.zh: 我长大了想当医生。

examples.en: I want to be a doctor when I grow up.
examples.zh: 我长大了想当医生。

examples.en: You should have a doctor take a look at it.
examples.zh: 你应该让个医生看看。

words.tran: 博士的；博士学位的；有博士学位的

syno.tran: 修理；窜改，伪造；为…治病；授以博士学位

drama.definition: n. an episode that is turbulent or highly emotional\nn. the literary genre of works intended for the theater\nn. the quality of being arresting or highly emotional
drama.translation: n. 戏剧, 戏剧艺术

examples.en: Wan-chun’s a total drama addict — Korean, American, she watches them all.
examples.zh: 婉君超爱追剧，韩剧、美剧她都看。

examples.en: They made the novel into a drama.
examples.zh: 他们把这本小说变成戏剧。

examples.en: Which drama series do you like best?
examples.zh: 你最喜欢什么电视剧？

words.tran: 戏剧的；引人注目的；激动人心的
编剧法的，戏剧作法的；演出的
演剧活动；演剧技术；业余演戏；戏剧性行为
戏剧化；可改编成剧本（等于dramatize）
使戏剧化；编写剧本；改编成戏剧
把…戏剧化；生动地表达（等于dramatize）

syno.tran: 戏剧，戏剧艺术；剧本；戏剧性事件

phrase.cn: 戏剧女皇；喜欢小题大做的人
n. 戏剧学校，戏剧专科学校

dream.definition:
n. a series of mental images and emotions occurring during sleep
n. imaginative thoughts indulged in while awake
n. a state of mind characterized by abstraction and release from reality
n. someone or something wonderful
dream.translation: n. 梦, 空想, 愿望\nv. 做梦, 想象, 梦想

examples.en: I want to explore the world. It’s my dream.
examples.zh: 我想要去探索世界。那是我的梦想。

examples.en: Little did I dream that I would see you here.
examples.zh: 我做梦也没有想过会在这里踫到你。

examples.en: It was John who helped make her dream come true.
examples.zh: 是约翰让她的梦想成真。

words.tran: 梦想的；空幻的；轻柔的；恍惚的
梦多地；经常容易梦见地
梦似地，朦胧地；爱梦想地
梦想家；做梦的人；不切实际的人
多梦；朦胧；梦幻状态；耽于幻想

syno.tran: 梦的；理想的；不切实际的

phrase.cn: 毫不费力地；轻而易举地；完美地

drop.definition:
n. a shape that is spherical and small
n. a small indefinite quantity (especially of a liquid)
n. a sudden sharp decrease in some quantity
n. a predetermined hiding place for the deposit and distribution of illicit goods (such as drugs or stolen property)
drop.translation:
n. 滴, 微量, 落下, 空投
vi. 放下, 掉下, 下降
vt. 使滴下, 放下, 丢失, 遗漏
[计] 投入, 投入点, 接入点, 分接点

examples.en: Drop me a line as soon as you get there.
examples.zh: 到了那儿之后跟我说一声儿。

examples.en: Please drop in at my house on your way home.
examples.zh: 你回家途中顺道来看看我吧。

examples.en: I'll drop by the post office on the way home.
examples.zh: 我会在回家的路上顺便去邮局。

words.tran: 滴管；使滴下的东西；点滴器
下降，减少；掉下，滴下（drop的过去式和过去分词形式）
落下；退出（drop的ing形式）；滴入；随口漏出

syno.tran: 滴；使降低；使终止；随口漏出

darling.definition: n. a special loved one\nn. an Australian river; tributary of the Murray River
darling.translation: n. 亲爱的, 可爱的人, 可爱的物\na. 可爱的, 亲爱的

examples.en: What are you doing, darling?
examples.zh: 你在做什么呢，亲爱的？

examples.en: Let's dance, my darling.
examples.zh: 亲爱的，我们跳舞吧。

examples.en: I'm sorry darling, you are merely a single tree in a forest, I just can't drop everything for you.
examples.zh: 不好意思美女，我不会为了你这一颗树，放弃一片森林。

datum.definition: n. an item of factual information derived from measurement or research
datum.translation: n. 论据, 材料, 资料, 已知数\n[医] 材料, 资料, 论据

examples.en: A tide gauge measures changes in sea level relative to a datum (a height reference).

daylight.translation: n. 白昼, 日光\nvt. 使沐浴于日光\nvi. 享有日光

examples.en: He had his car stolen in broad daylight.
examples.zh: 他的车子光天化日被偷走了。

examples.en: Today, robbers robbed another bank in broad daylight.
examples.zh: 今天强盗大白天的就抢了另一家银行。

examples.en: Daylight savings is over today.
examples.zh: 今天夏令时结束了。

deafen.definition: v. be unbearably loud\nv. make or render deaf\nv. make soundproof

examples.en: With a deafening roar, the rocket was hurled into space.
The dinosaur continued to roar at a deafening volume.
The roar of the heavy guns was deafening.

death.definition:
n. the event of dying or departure from life
n. the permanent end of all life functions in an organism or part of an organism
n. the absence of life or state of being dead
n. the time when something ends

examples.en: He hasn't got over the death of his wife yet.
examples.zh: 他还没有从妻子去世的悲痛中恢复过来。

examples.en: They demanded the king be put to death at once.
examples.zh: 他们要求马上把国王处死。

examples.en: The death of Ronnie James Dio made me very sad.
examples.zh: Ronnie James Dio的死让我非常难过。

decidedly.definition: r. without question and beyond doubt
decidedly.translation: adv. 决定了, 坚决, 明显, 显而易见, 显然, 明确, 果断, 毫无疑问

examples.en: Black cutty pipes are decidedly in bad form.
The atmosphere in the room was decidedly frosty.
She felt decidedly uncomfortable faced with the old woman’s frosty manner.

decision.definition:
n. the act of making up your mind about something
n. a position or opinion or judgment reached after consideration
n. (boxing) a victory won on points when no knockout has occurred
n. the outcome of a game or contest
decision.translation: n. 决定, 决心, 决断\n[计] 判定

examples.en: We are waiting for him to make another decision.
examples.zh: 我们在等他做另一个决定。

examples.en: You make a decision for yourself on this matter.
examples.zh: 这件事你自己决定就是了。

examples.en: Why didn't you consult me before taking this decision?
examples.zh: 你做这个决定之前，为什么不先问过我？

decorative.definition: s serving an esthetic rather than a useful purpose

examples.en: Ivy is a decorative plant that causes a few problems.
Rosemaling is a style of decorative painting developed in Norway.
She piped decorative borders on the cake with icing.

defence.definition:
n (psychiatry) an unconscious process that tries to reduce the anxiety associated with instinctive desires
n (sports) the team that is trying to prevent the other team from scoring
n the defendant and his legal advisors collectively
n an organization of defenders that provides resistance against attack
n the speech act of answering an attack on your assertions
n the justification for some act or belief
n a structure used to defend against attack
n a defendant's answer or plea denying the truth of the charges against him
n (military) military action or resources protecting a country against potential enemies
n protection from harm
n the act of defending someone or something against attack or injury
defence.translation: n. 防卫, 防卫设备\n[经] (诉讼程序中的)辩护

examples.en: Ignorance of the law is not accepted as a defence.
The defence attorney achieved a plea deal of ILS 5 million.
That Georgian forward is a nightmare for the opposing defence.

deferential.translation: a. 恭敬的\n[医] 输精管的

examples.en: Ziri was always deferential around Rima's mother.
Tom was too deferential.

definitely.definition: r without question and beyond doubt
definitely.translation: adv. 明确无疑地, 清楚地

examples.en: This year is definitely a special year in human history.
examples.zh: 今年肯定是人类历史上特殊的一年。

examples.en: We can now say definitely that this hypothesis holds water.
examples.zh: 我们现在能肯定地说，这个假设是成立的。

examples.en: Tom says that Mary definitely won't accept the job.
examples.zh: 汤姆说玛丽绝不会接受这工作。

deflection.definition: n. a twist or aberration; especially a perverse or abnormal way of judging or acting\nn. the amount by which a propagating wave is bent\nn. the movement of the pointer or pen of a measuring instrument from its zero position
deflection.translation: n. 歪斜, 偏, 偏向\n[医] 偏向, 偏离, 偏转(光), 偏转, 波(心电图)

examples.en: The calculated deflection at the end of the beam is 2 cm.
The general theory of relativity predicted the deflection of starlight by the Sun.
A meteor exploded over Russia, yet no one cares enough to provide funding for meteor deflection technology.

deform.definition: v. make formless\nv. become misshapen\nv. alter the shape of (something) by stress
deform.translation: vt. 使残缺, 使变形\nvi. 变形

examples.en: A lozenge is a square deformed indefinably, generally by heat.
Alberto saw some weird deformed guy watching him in the woods.
In ancient Sparta, they threw children born deformed off a cliff.

deformation.definition: n. alteration in the shape or dimensions of an object as a result of the application of stress to it
deformation.translation: n. 损形, 变丑, 畸形\n[化] 变形; 形变

degradation.definition: n. changing to a lower state (a less respected state)
degradation.translation: n. 降格, 堕落, 退化\n[计] 降级

examples.en: Will humanity be able to prevent the degradation of ecosystems?
Overgrazing is leading to extreme soil degradation in Algeria.
In all four, degradation can be clearly observed.

demography.definition: n. the branch of sociology that studies the characteristics of human populations
demography.translation: n. 人口统计学\n[医] 人口学, 人口统计学

examples.en: Tom just finished writing a 300-page treatise on demography.
"What's demonography?" "That says demography, Tom."
Due to its geography and demography, conquering Panjshir by force is considered extremely difficult.

dependant.definition: n. a person who relies on another person for support (especially financial support)
dependant.translation: n. 家眷, 侍从, 食客\n[法] 受赡养人, 家庭负担

examples.en: When applying for a student loan you must report any dependants.
Space technology will remain dependant on national governments unless we find a way to make space profitable.

deposition.definition: n. the natural process of laying down a deposit of something\nn. (law) a pretrial interrogation of a witness; usually conducted in a lawyer's office\nn. the act of deposing someone; removing a powerful person from a position or office
deposition.translation: n. 免职, 作证, 沉淀\n[化] 沉积

examples.en: Sputter deposition is widely employed in the semiconductor industry.
This is a deposition. You answer the questions truthfully but never volunteer anything.
Does the landlord want a deposition?

derivation.definition: n. the source or origin from which something derives (i.e. comes or issues)\nn. a line of reasoning that shows how a conclusion follows logically from accepted propositions\nn. (descriptive linguistics) the process whereby new words are formed from existing words or bases by affixation
derivation.translation: n. 推论, 推导, 来历\n[医] 衍化, 诱导

examples.en: Esperanto has an excellent derivation system.
The derivations of many words are unknown.
Some people find derivation to be more logical and regular in Ido than in Esperanto.

desperately.translation: adv. 拼命地；绝望地；极度地

examples.en: She needed money desperately.
examples.zh: 她迫切地需要钱。

despite.translation: n. 轻视, 憎恨\nprep. 虽然, 尽管

examples.en: Despite a lot of difficulties, he still completed the task.
examples.zh: 虽然困难重重，他还是完成了这个任务。

examples.en: The teachers are all continuing to teach despite the immense pressure.
examples.zh: 老师们都顶著巨大的压力在坚持上课。

examples.en: Despite different languages and cultures, everyone still became friends.
examples.zh: 尽管语言和习俗不同，大家还是能够成为朋友。

determination.definition: n. the act of determining the properties of something, usually by research or calculation\nn. the quality of being determined to do or achieve something; firmness of purpose\nn. deciding or controlling something's outcome or nature
determination.translation: n. 决心, 果断\n[化] 判定; 测定

examples.en: The soul is made up of reason, determination, and passion.
examples.zh: 灵魂是由理性、意志和情欲构成的。

examples.en: He made a determination to be a doctor.
examples.zh: 他下定了决心要做医生。

examples.en: We've got to have determination.
examples.zh: 我们要下决心了。

devil.definition: n. an evil supernatural being\nn. a word used in exclamations of confusion\nv. coat or stuff with a spicy paste
devil.translation: n. 魔鬼\nvt. 折磨, 戏弄

examples.en: Speak of the devil and he is sure to appear.
examples.zh: 说曹操，曹操就到。

examples.en: Don't shoot the devil in the back. You might miss.
examples.zh: 别射撒旦的背部。你可能会射不中。

examples.en: The man sold his soul to the devil.
examples.zh: 这人把灵魂卖给魔鬼。

diagnostic.definition: a. concerned with diagnosis; used for furthering diagnosis\ns. characteristic or indicative of a disease
diagnostic.translation: a. 诊断的, 有助于诊断的, 特征的\nn. 诊断, 病的征候, 诊断法\n[计] 诊断的

examples.en: We use the latest diagnostic and treatment methods.
The sphygmomanometer is an important diagnostic instrument.

dialog.definition: n a conversation between two persons\nn the lines spoken by characters in drama or fiction\nn a literary composition in the form of a conversation between two people
dialog.translation: n. 会话, 对话\n[计] 对话

examples.en: I did not participate in the dialog.
examples.zh: 我没有参与对话。

directly.definition: r. without deviation\nr. without anyone or anything intervening\nr. in a forthright manner; candidly or frankly
directly.translation: adv. 径直地, 直接地, 直率地, 正好地, 直截了当地, (非正式)立即, 马上\nconj. 一...(就...), 一当...就...\n[计] 直接的

examples.en: The English ambassador demanded to meet with the President directly.
examples.zh: 英国大使要求直接会见总统。

examples.en: If you want to know, just ask directly.
examples.zh: 如果您想知道，直接问就是了。

examples.en: The infrastructure of an application is directly related to its overall performance.
examples.zh: 一个应用的架构直接关系到它的整体性能。

director.definition: n. someone who controls resources and expenditures\nn. member of a board of directors\nn. someone who supervises the actors and directs the action in the production of a show
director.translation: n. 主管, 导演, 董事\n[计] 寻向偶极子; 指挥仪

examples.en: This is Professor Oak, the director of this experiment.
examples.zh: 这位是奥克教授，他是这项实验的负责人。

examples.en: Even Dwarfs Started Small is a 1970 film by German director Werner Herzog.
examples.zh: "侏儒流氓"是德国导演韦纳荷索在一九七零年的一部电影。

examples.en: He is a talented young director.
examples.zh: 他是个富有才能的年轻导演。

disagreement.definition: n. a conflict of people's opinions or actions or characters\nn. the speech act of disagreeing or arguing or disputing
disagreement.translation: n. 不合, 争论, 不一致\n[法] 不一致, 不同意, 陪审团的意见不一

examples.en: It's clear that there's a rather strong disagreement between the two.
examples.zh: 很明显的是这两者之间有很强烈的分歧。

examples.en: They express disagreement by shaking their heads, which may indicate agreement in other countries.
examples.zh: 他们以摇头表示不同意，而其他国家的人可能以摇头表示同意。

examples.en: Jim sometimes has disagreements with his wife.
examples.zh: 吉姆有时与他的妻子意见分歧。

disappearance.definition: n. the act of leaving secretly or without explanation\nn. the event of passing out of sight\nn. ceasing to exist
disappearance.translation: n. 看不见, 失踪, 消失

examples.en: We have to look into the disappearance of the doctor.
examples.zh: 我们必须调查医生的失踪案。

examples.en: The police now believe Tom had something to do with Mary's disappearance.
examples.zh: 警方现在认为汤姆和玛丽的失踪有干系。

examples.en: The police now believe that Tom had something to do with Mary's disappearance.
examples.zh: 警方现在认为汤姆和玛丽的失踪有干系。

discontented.definition: a. showing or experiencing dissatisfaction or restless longing

examples.en: Tom told me that he thought that Mary was discontented.
Tom and Mary told me that they were discontented.
Tom told me that he thought Mary was discontented.

dishonour.definition:
n a state of shame or disgrace
n lacking honor or integrity
v bring shame or dishonor upon
v force (someone) to have sex against their will
v refuse to accept
dishonour.translation: n. 不名誉, 使人丢脸的人/事, 耻辱, 不光彩\nvt. 使丧失名誉, 使受耻辱, 使丢脸, 奸污, 拒收, 无法偿付, 拒付

examples.en: You wanted to avoid war at the price of dishonour.
Such dishonour can only be washed away with blood.
There is less dishonour in my death than in life as you propose it to me.

disillusioned.translation: a. 幻想破灭了的, 大失所望的, 醒悟了的

examples.en: Is there a place that promises peace to disillusioned souls?
William became disillusioned with his decision to rob a bank.
Blessed is the one who expects nothing, never being disillusioned.

disk.definition: n. something with a round shape resembling a flat circular plate\nn. a flat circular plate
disk.translation: n. 圆盘, 磁盘\n[计] 磁盘

examples.en: I've formatted your hard disk by mistake.
examples.zh: 我不小心格式化了你的硬盘。

examples.en: My son followed Xiao Wang to buy disks.
examples.zh: 我儿子跟着小王买碟片去了。

examples.en: Floppy disks are the predecessor of hard disks.
examples.zh: 软盘是硬盘的前身。

disobedience.definition: n. the failure to obey\nn. the trait of being unwilling to obey
disobedience.translation: n. 不服从, 不孝, 违反

examples.en: The Catalan politicians are accused of disobedience, embezzlement, and malfeasance.
He couldn't suffer the slightest disobedience in his men.
Your willful disobedience is what got you here.

disorient.definition: v. cause to be lost or disoriented
disorient.translation: vt. 使失去方向, 使迷惑

examples.en: Tom said I looked disoriented.
examples.zh: 汤姆说我看起来很迷茫。

displacement.definition: n. (chemistry) a reaction in which an elementary substance displaces and sets free a constituent element from a compound\nn. (psychiatry) a defense mechanism that transfers affect or reaction from the original object to some more acceptable one\nn. to move something from its natural environment
displacement.translation: n. 换置, 移位, 移动, 取代\n[化] 顶替展开法

examples.en: Many adults missed out on schooling because of warfare and displacement.
Displacements should be kept to a strict minimum.
The ongoing conflict in Afghanistan has led to widespread displacement, economic hardship, and infrastructural damage.

displease.translation: v. 使不愉快, 使(人)生气

examples.en: If she was displeased, she never showed it.
examples.zh: 如果她不高兴, 她从来不表现出来。

examples.en: Tom must have been displeased.
examples.zh: 汤姆一定很不高兴。

examples.en: Tom must've been displeased.
examples.zh: 汤姆一定很不高兴。

disruptive.definition: s. characterized by unrest or disorder or insubordination
disruptive.translation: a. 分裂的, 破坏(性)的\n[计] 击穿的, 中断的

examples.en: Temper tantrums are unpleasant and disruptive behaviours or emotional outbursts.
Working shifts can be extremely disruptive to family life.
Tom is often disruptive in class.

dissatisfaction.definition: n. the feeling of being displeased and discontent

examples.en: The residents expressed their dissatisfaction at the noise.
examples.zh: 居民们对噪音表示了不满。

examples.en: Her remarks caused dissatisfaction in the public.
examples.zh: 她的言论引起了舆论的不满。

dissatisfy.translation: vt. 使感觉不满, 不满足

examples.en: If you're so dissatisfied with what I'm doing, you'd be better off doing it yourself.
examples.zh: 你要是这么不满意我做的，自己来做好了。

disservice.definition: n. an act intended to help that turns out badly
disservice.translation: n. 伤害, 帮倒忙的行为

examples.en: What Tom is doing is a disservice to the community.
Don't do yourself the disservice of not watching this film.
I think they did you a great disservice.

distinctly.definition: r. clear to the mind; with distinct mental discernment\nr. in a distinct and distinguishable manner\nr. to a distinct degree
distinctly.translation: adv. 显然地, 明显地, 清楚地

examples.en: Igor distinctly heard Anna screaming: "No! Please don't do that!"
We could distinctly hear Kabyle music coming from the second floor.
I distinctly remember hearing the clock on the mantelpiece strike two.

dorm.definition: n a college or university building containing living quarters for students

examples.en: Have you gotten used to living in the dorm?
examples.zh: 你习惯在宿舍生活了吗？

examples.en: You'll get used to the dorm life pretty quickly.
examples.zh: 你很快会适应在宿舍的生活的。

examples.en: Renmei is waiting for Xueyou in the dorm.
examples.zh: 人美在宿舍等着学友呢。

doubtless.translation: a. 无疑的, 确定的\nadv. 无疑地, 确定地

examples.en: You doubtless mean well; but your ideas are unhappily mistaken.
He was evidently unconscious, doubtless in an anaesthetised sleep.
It is doubtless that he was murdered.

downstairs.definition: a. on or of lower floors of a building\nr. on a floor below
downstairs.translation: n. 楼下\na. 楼下的\nadv. 在楼下

examples.en: I went downstairs and turned off the light.
examples.zh: 我下楼把灯关了。

examples.en: Someone is waiting for you downstairs.
examples.zh: 楼下有人在等您。

examples.en: Mary, you've come at just the right time! Help me carry this sofa downstairs.
examples.zh: 玛丽，你来得正是时候！来帮我把这张沙发搬到楼下！

downward.definition: s. on or toward a surface regarded as a base

examples.en: I was looking downward to the bottom of the valley.
The climber fell 100 meters downward and broke both his legs.
We risk tilting ourselves into a downward spiral of defeatism.

dozen.definition: n the cardinal number that is the sum of eleven and one\ns denoting a quantity consisting of 12 items or units
dozen.translation: n. 打, 十二个\na. 一打的

examples.en: In U.S. bakeries, a "baker's dozen" is 13, not 12.
examples.zh: 在美国的面包店，"面包师傅的一打"是13，不是12。

examples.en: About a dozen trees had soon been planted.
examples.zh: 十几棵树很快就种好了。

examples.en: Several dozen young people participated in the demonstration.
examples.zh: 几十个年轻人参加了示威游行。

drawer.definition: n. a boxlike container in a piece of furniture; made so as to slide in and out\nn. the person who writes a check or draft instructing the drawee to pay someone else
drawer.translation: n. 抽屉, 开票人\n[计] 抽屉

examples.en: There should be a box of matches in the top drawer.
examples.zh: 最上面的抽屉里应该有一盒火柴。

examples.en: There is a pair of worn red stockings in the drawer.
examples.zh: 抽屉里有一双穿过的红色丝袜。

examples.en: Tom took a spatula out of the drawer.
examples.zh: 汤姆从抽屉里拿出一把锅铲。

drawing.definition:
n. an illustration that is drawn by hand and published in a book, magazine, or newspaper
n. a representation of forms or objects on a surface by means of lines
n. the creation of artistic pictures or diagrams
n. act of getting or draining something such as electricity or a liquid from a source
drawing.translation: n. 图画, 制图, 拉\n[计] 绘图

examples.en: "Drawing dragons and dotting in the eyes" is a fable.
examples.zh: 画龙点睛是一则寓言故事。

examples.en: I'm not good at drawing, but I can write.
examples.zh: 我不擅长画画，但我会写文章。

examples.en: Drawing is a lot of fun; it helps me to relax.
examples.zh: 画画能带给我很多乐趣，也能让我放松自己。

examples.en: The consequences of Sendai's earthquake were dreadful!
examples.zh: 仙台地震的结果很恐怖。

drunk.translation: a. 喝醉了的\ndrink的过去式

examples.en: I admit, at that time I was a little drunk.
examples.zh: 我承认当时是有点醉。

examples.en: He was drunk and forgot to shut the back door.
examples.zh: 他醉得忘了把门关上。

examples.en: Tom was so drunk that he didn't even recognize me.
examples.zh: 汤姆醉得连我都认不出来了。

duke.definition: n. a British peer of the highest rank\nn. a nobleman (in various countries) of high rank

examples.en: Did the Duke of Zhou dream of the butterfly, or did the butterfly dream of the Duke of Zhou?
examples.zh: 究竟是周公梦到了蝴蝶，还是蝴蝶梦到了周公？

dully.definition: r. without liveliness\nr. without luster or shine
dully.translation: adv. 钝地, 迟钝地, 不清楚地

examples.en: From time to time lightning flashes, and thunder rumbles dully.

dying.definition: a. in or associated with the process of passing from life or ceasing to be
dying.translation: a. 垂死的\n[法] 快要死的, 垂死的, 临终的

examples.en: The survivors were found on an island, dying of starvation.
examples.zh: 幸存者在一个岛上被找到了，已经饿得要死了。

examples.en: There were cars burning, people dying, and nobody could help them.
examples.zh: 有着火的汽车和垂死的人，而且没有人能帮得上忙。

examples.en: As soon as man is born, he begins to die.
examples.zh: 从出生的一刻开始，我们就在步向死亡。

dynamo.definition: n. generator consisting of a coil (the armature) that rotates between the poles of an electromagnet (the field magnet) causing a current to flow in the armature
dynamo.translation: n. 发电机\n[医] 电机, 发电机

examples.en: Mary is the dynamo behind the company's most recent innovation.
I have a keyring with a carabiner and a dynamo lamp.
I have a keyring with a carabiner with a dynamo lamp.
